title: Mencius argued that a child near a well shows we are born good
body: The Confucian thinker Mencius, of the 4th century BC, asked readers to imagine suddenly seeing a small child about to fall into a well. Anyone would feel instant alarm, he said, not to impress the parents or neighbors, but spontaneously. Such reactions are ‘sprouts’ of compassion, shame, respect and moral judgment that must be cultivated like plants. The later Confucian Xunzi argued instead that human nature is bad.

slides.heading: From a child at a well to a theory of human nature

steps.label: A child is about to fall into a well
Not for praise or reward: it is spontaneous
So compassion is a sprout we are born with
Tended like a plant, it grows into virtue

slides.question: Why did Mencius stress that the alarm at the well is spontaneous?
options: Goodness is innate, not put on for show
We act mainly from fear of punishment
slides.explanation: The alarm comes before any thought of impressing parents or neighbors, so Mencius read it as a ‘sprout’ of compassion that must be cultivated like a plant.

slides.heading: Mencius’s four sprouts: match each feeling to its virtue
slides.explanation: Mencius said people have these four beginnings just as they have four limbs; each must be cultivated.
